title: Business continuity management program and policy
status_rationale: No production service, no adopted continuity policy and no exercise records exist as of 2026-11-25 (architecture/ECHELON-CURRENT-STATE-BRIEF.md).
target_answer: Echelon operates a business continuity management program aligned with ISO 22301 concepts. A board-approved policy covers every customer-facing service and the functions that support it, names an accountable executive, is reviewed at least annually and on material change, and its summary and change log are available to customers under NDA. Continuity evidence (BIA, plans, exercises, remediation) is generated in a governed repository with provenance so that customers can verify freshness rather than rely on an annual attestation.
current_practice: Not established. The business plan (13.06) states an intent to test recovery and record evidence; no continuity policy, owner or review record was located.
intended_practice: Adopt a continuity policy before the first customer contract; record approvals in Praxis-governed repositories; publish a customer-facing summary.
provable: Nothing. Only planning text in the business plan and Unbound requirements UNB-GAP-028, UNB-OPS-001 and SOC2-015.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet adopted a business continuity policy. We plan to adopt one, aligned with ISO 22301 concepts, before any production customer goes live, and to share a summary under NDA.
owner: Proposed: Business Continuity Owner (role not yet staffed)
open_questions: Who is the accountable executive for continuity, and does a board or equivalent body exist to approve the policy?

title: Business impact analysis and criticality
status_rationale: No production service, no adopted continuity policy and no exercise records exist as of 2026-11-25 (architecture/ECHELON-CURRENT-STATE-BRIEF.md).
target_answer: Every capability has a BIA entry stating customer consequence over time (for example missed grant deadlines, unreceipted year-end contributions, blocked payroll-like disbursements to charities), maximum tolerable disruption, minimum acceptable service, and dependencies including cloud, identity, payment rails, custodians, charity data sources and AI model providers. Recovery objectives are derived from the BIA, and Echelon provides each financial customer with the information needed to classify Unbound in its own BIA and critical-vendor inventory.
current_practice: Not established. Unbound requirements call for per-capability failure modes (UNB-RES-001) and per-data-class recovery objectives (RR-UNB-RES-003-r2) but no BIA has been performed.
intended_practice: Perform a BIA as part of architecture acceptance; gate capability activation on a reviewed BIA entry.
customer_statement: A business impact analysis has not yet been performed. Our design requirements call for one per capability, and we plan to provide its results to customers for use in their own impact analyses.
owner: Proposed: Business Continuity Owner (role not yet staffed)

title: Continuity plans, alternate communications and crisis notification
status_rationale: No production service, no adopted continuity policy and no exercise records exist as of 2026-11-25 (architecture/ECHELON-CURRENT-STATE-BRIEF.md).
target_answer: Scenario plans exist for loss of people, technology, facilities and providers. Each plan names decision authority, customer and regulator-facing communication steps and alternate channels that do not depend on the production platform, its email domain or its identity provider. Current copies are held out of band and checked automatically for drift. Customers receive a designated contact list and the channels Echelon will use if its primary domain is compromised.
intended_practice: Draft plans with the BIA; store a signed out-of-band copy; register alternate channels with each customer at onboarding.
customer_statement: Continuity plans have not yet been written. We plan scenario-based plans with alternate communication channels that work when our primary systems are unavailable.
owner: Proposed: Business Continuity Owner (role not yet staffed)

title: Continuity exercises and testing
status_rationale: No production service, no adopted continuity policy and no exercise records exist as of 2026-11-25 (architecture/ECHELON-CURRENT-STATE-BRIEF.md).
target_answer: Plans are exercised at least annually with scenario variety, including correlated conjunctions (year-end surge plus payment-provider outage plus custodian delay), and customers may observe or participate in a joint exercise annually. Each exercise produces a dated report with measured timings, findings and remediation closure evidence; summaries are shared under NDA.
current_practice: Not established. TVR-OPS-003 specifies a year-end readiness plan with conjunction drills; no drill has run.
intended_practice: Run a first tabletop before production; add functional exercises once a production-like environment exists.
customer_statement: No continuity exercises have been conducted because no production service exists. We plan annual exercises, including joint exercises with customers who request them.
owner: Proposed: Business Continuity Owner (role not yet staffed)

title: Key-person and founder dependence
status_rationale: Headcount, ownership and succession arrangements are not established in records reviewed. The business plan (11.09) treats founder dependence as a concentration risk to be decomposed, which indicates the dependence exists.
target_answer: No capability, credential or decision depends on a single individual. A key-person register lists each capability with a named alternate; emergency credentials are held under dual control or split custody; the codebase, requirements, decisions and operating procedures are in governed repositories with provenance so a qualified successor can operate and change the system; and portability is proven by exercises in which the primary does not participate. Contracts give customers a verifiable exit package and transition assistance if Echelon cannot continue.
current_practice: Unknown. The business plan identifies founder dependence as a risk and proposes capability decomposition and portability tests (11.09); no register, alternate or portability test was located.
intended_practice: Build the key-person register at formation; place emergency credentials under dual control; run a portability test before the first production customer.
provable: Repositories under Praxis governance exist with provenance records, which supports knowledge portability, but no portability test has been run.
customer_statement: Echelon is an early-stage organization and acknowledges key-person dependence as a material risk. We plan to document alternates, place critical credentials under dual control and test that others can operate the service before going live.
owner: Proposed: Chief Executive (role holder not established)

challenge.customer_intent: Avoid losing a critical service because one person, typically the founder, becomes unavailable.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Service cannot be operated, repaired or recovered; credentials are lost; customer data or payment authority is stranded.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional answers (key-person insurance, an org chart showing a deputy) provide money or names but not working capability; they rarely prove a successor can actually operate the system.
challenge.legally_required: No. Supervisory guidance (FFIEC, interagency TPRM) expects financial institutions to assess vendor concentration and viability; it does not impose staffing levels on the vendor.
challenge.contractually_required: Sometimes, as step-in rights, escrow, or transition assistance clauses in bank and enterprise contracts.
challenge.historical_convention: Buyers ask for headcount and backup staff because larger vendors could show them.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Partial. Governed repositories, reproducible builds, infrastructure as code and AI-agent-executable runbooks can make operational knowledge portable, and a customer-held exit package removes data-stranding risk.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Dual-control credential custody can be enforced by the identity provider and cloud organization policy.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Praxis provenance shows who changed what; a periodic portability exercise produces dated evidence that an alternate succeeded.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Prove portability by exercise and give customers a verifiable exit package, instead of asserting headcount.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, through exercise reports and exit-package rehearsals the customer can verify.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If portability depends on AI agents that themselves depend on one person's accounts or one provider, or if documentation drifts from the running system.
challenge.alternative_risks: Documentation and agent runbooks may give false confidence if exercises are not realistic.
supporting_arguments: Working capability is what the customer needs, not headcount.
Exit packages address the worst outcome directly.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain. Bank procurement scores small vendors on headcount and financial viability regardless of portability evidence.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: A successor without tacit knowledge may still fail under incident pressure.
Regulators and procurement officers may treat a single-founder vendor as unacceptable for critical services regardless of evidence.

title: Workforce disruption and pandemic readiness
status_rationale: No production service, no adopted continuity policy and no exercise records exist as of 2026-11-25 (architecture/ECHELON-CURRENT-STATE-BRIEF.md).
target_answer: All operational roles can be performed remotely on managed devices with no dependency on a single office or data center under Echelon's control. The plan defines minimum staffing per function, absenteeism triggers and which non-essential work is suspended, and identifies the share of operational work performed by AI agents under human supervision, including what happens if supervising staff are unavailable.
current_practice: Not established. Echelon appears to have no physical facility dependency, but this is not documented.
intended_practice: Document remote-operation and staffing thresholds with the continuity plan.
customer_statement: We have not yet documented a pandemic or workforce-disruption plan. We intend to operate without dependence on any single office.

title: Dependence on AI providers for engineering, operations and runtime
status_rationale: Echelon intends AI agents to perform engineering and operations work and Unbound requirements route some decisions to AI (REQ-X-017); no dependency inventory or fallback test exists.
target_answer: AI is never in the authoritative path for money movement, authority, holds or records: deterministic policy evaluates first and AI is advisory, so a model-provider outage degrades throughput and convenience but not correctness. Each AI-dependent function has a named fallback (alternate model, human queue, or deferral) tested quarterly with the provider disabled. Engineering can continue at reduced velocity without AI agents because the codebase is conventional F#/.NET under human review. Model versions are pinned and provider deprecations are tracked as change events.
current_practice: Not established. Requirements REQ-X-017 (rules first, AI second, human third), UNB-RES-001 (model outage failure modes) and UNB-CTL-006 (correlated AI failures) describe the intended design.
intended_practice: Inventory AI dependencies; implement rules-first routing; test with providers disabled.
customer_statement: Our design keeps AI out of the authoritative path for payments and approvals so that an AI provider outage cannot cause incorrect financial actions. This is a design intent; it has not been built or tested.

challenge.adverse_outcome: Stalled grant vetting at year-end, unreviewable decisions, or engineering unable to ship a security fix.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional vendor continuity reviews look at the AI provider's SOC report and uptime, which does not address model behavior change or deprecation.
challenge.legally_required: No statute requires it for Echelon. EU DORA requires EU financial entities to manage ICT concentration risk, which includes AI services they rely on indirectly.
challenge.contractually_required: Increasingly requested in AI addenda; not yet standard.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Yes within scope: if authoritative state changes cannot depend on AI output, provider failure cannot corrupt financial state.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Type-level separation of advisory AI outputs from authoritative commands can be enforced in F# domain types and tested.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Scheduled provider-disabled test runs produce dated results.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Architectural exclusion of AI from authority, plus tested fallbacks, rather than reliance on provider assurances.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Partly: test results and code review can show it; customers cannot easily inspect the type boundary themselves.

challenge.alternative_risks: Human fallback capacity for AI-assisted vetting may be insufficient at year-end volume.
supporting_arguments: Correctness does not depend on a third party.
Model churn becomes a throughput issue, not an integrity issue.

title: Alternate processing for grants and payments during platform outage
status_rationale: No production service, no adopted continuity policy and no exercise records exist as of 2026-11-25 (architecture/ECHELON-CURRENT-STATE-BRIEF.md).
target_answer: The sponsor, not Unbound, originates payments, so the sponsor can always pay an urgent grant through its own bank channel. Unbound provides a documented alternate procedure, an offline read-only archive of fund balances and pending grants, and an OutOfBandPaymentRecorded command that, after recovery, cancels the matching queued instruction and registers the expected bank debit, so no duplicate payment is sent. Manual processing preserves the sponsor's dual approval and sanctions screening through a checklist, and replay of queued requests occurs only after reconciliation and revalidation.
current_practice: Not established. Requirements CNV-PAY-001, CNV-PLT-007 and REQ-X-006 specify the design.
intended_practice: Implement the OutOfBandPaymentRecorded command and offline archive before payment features launch; drill annually with each sponsor.
customer_statement: Unbound is designed so the sponsor keeps payment authority and can pay through its own bank during an outage, with recorded reconciliation afterwards. This has not been built or tested.

challenge.customer_intent: Keep urgent grants and disbursements flowing if the platform is down.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Charities miss funding; donors miss deadlines; duplicate payments occur after recovery.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Vendors usually promise faster recovery. Fast recovery does not help a sponsor during the outage and does not address duplicates after recovery.
challenge.legally_required: No for Echelon. FINRA Rule 4370 requires member firms to plan for customers' prompt access to funds; that applies to the customer if it is a member firm.
challenge.contractually_required: Common in bank contracts as alternate processing provisions.
challenge.historical_convention: Banks expect alternate processing sites for core processors.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Partly: because the sponsor originates payments (CNV-PAY-001), the platform is never the only path to pay.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Duplicate prevention via idempotency keys and the out-of-band cancellation command.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Sponsor-retained authority plus deterministic reconciliation instead of an alternate processing site.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If a sponsor has outsourced its bank operations entirely to the platform or lacks bank channel access.
challenge.alternative_risks: Manual processing may skip sanctions screening or dual approval unless checklists are followed.
supporting_arguments: Removes the platform as a single point of failure for payments.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain; some sponsors lack staff to execute manual payments.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Shifts operational burden to the customer during a crisis.
Manual processes are where fraud tends to occur.

title: Subprocessor continuity and Echelon viability

target_answer: Critical subprocessors (cloud, managed PostgreSQL, payment connectivity, identity, AI providers) are inventoried with assurance reports, bridge letters and reviewed continuity commitments. intended_practice: Build the vendor register at provider selection; implement exit package before production; evaluate escrow providers.

challenge.contractually_required: Escrow is common in bank and public-sector contracts for critical software.
challenge.historical_convention: Escrow dates from on-premises licensed software.

challenge.stronger_alternative: Continuous verifiable data portability plus documented successor-operator procedures.

challenge.alternative_risks: Data without software may still leave the customer unable to operate for months.
